articles.title: C3 Metals hits highest-grade copper-gold-silver mineralization yet at Peru Project
articles.description: C3 Metals CEO Dan Symons joined Steve Darling from Proactive to announce the highest-grade copper-gold-silver mineralization intersected to date at the company's Khaleesi copper project in southern Peru. The latest results come from drill hole KHZ5790-005, which intersected a broad zone of intense chalcopyrite mineralization hosted within the main magnetite skarn body currently being defined through the company's ongoing drilling program. Symons told Proactive that the hole was designed to test a magnetite and garnet skarn target in an area with limited previous drilling. The results returned 64.9 metres grading 2.53% copper, 0.87 grams per tonne gold and 11.6 g/t silver, with 6 parts per million molybdenum, starting at approximately 337.6 metres downhole. Within that interval, the company reported a higher-grade section of 23.3 metres grading 4.75% copper, 1.84 g/t gold and 20.4 g/t silver, with 5 ppm molybdenum. This interval returned a calculated copper equivalent grade of 6.64%. On a copper-equivalent basis, the broader intercept graded 3.45% CuEq, highlighting the potential for substantial higher-grade mineralization within the larger skarn system. Symons said the company is still at an early stage of understanding the geometry and overall extent of this higher-grade zone. C3 Metals is now systematically stepping out from the discovery in multiple directions to evaluate the continuity of the mineralization and determine its potential scale. The company is prioritizing step-out drilling at approximately 50- to 100-metre intervals to better define the geometry and distribution of the copper-gold-silver mineralization identified in KHZ5790-005. Alongside drilling, C3 Metals is advancing a series of geophysical surveys designed to improve its understanding of the broader geological system and identify additional exploration targets. Drone magnetic and gravity surveys covering approximately 1,500 hectares have recently been completed, with the data currently undergoing inversion. A three-dimensional induced polarization (3DIP) survey also began in late September and is expected to be completed during November 2026. The company plans to integrate the magnetic, gravity and 3DIP results into three-dimensional models alongside existing drill results, surface geology and exploration data. These models are expected to help identify concealed skarn mineralization and investigate the potential presence of an underlying porphyry source or causative intrusive system. articles.title: Ameriwest Critical Metals advances Bornite Copper-Gold Project with historic core review
articles.description: Ameriwest Critical Metals CEO David Watkins joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss the company's efforts to advance the Bornite copper-gold-silver project in Oregon, including the reassessment of historic drill core, plans for an updated technical report and opportunities for additional exploration. Watkins explained that the Bornite project was previously owned by Plexus Resources during the 1990s, when a pre-feasibility study and other technical work were completed. Ameriwest has since recovered a substantial portion of the historic drill core and transported it to Reno, Nevada, where the material is being logged and selected intervals resampled. The company has released results from the first three holes in a seven-hole resampling program. Watkins said the initial findings are generally consistent with historical results, with copper grades appearing somewhat higher and gold and silver values also showing improvements in several intervals. Additional assay results are expected as the remaining samples are processed, providing further information to compare against the original drilling data. The resampling initiative is designed to verify the historical exploration results and support the preparation of an updated technical report compliant with NI 43-101 standards. Ameriwest is targeting completion of that report in the first quarter of 2027. Alongside the technical work, the company is beginning the permitting process for additional confirmation drilling, which could take place next summer. A key focus is evaluating the potential of the project's breccia pipe deposit. Historical work identified a high-grade outer shell with grades exceeding 3% copper equivalent, while Ameriwest is also investigating whether the lower-grade interior portion of the structure could support economic mining under current metal price conditions. Watkins said the company is undertaking technical studies to determine whether the interior of the breccia pipe could have mining potential, emphasizing that the work is intended to test that geological and economic concept. Ameriwest is also considering geophysical surveys to investigate whether additional breccia pipes may exist elsewhere in the area. The work could help identify extensions of the known mineralization at depth and investigate the possibility of a deeper feeder system. “They must accept that they have no choice but to acknowledge the power of Iran,” said Nikzad. “It is the Americans, not the Iranian nation, who will ultimately surrender in this conflict. [Tehran] has no intention of negotiating on the nuclear issue regardless of any pressure."

The deputy speaker said that “this great nation has already granted its enemies ample opportunity for negotiations in this arena, but it was met only with repeated breaches of promises and the illegal bombardment of parts of its peaceful nuclear facilities”.

Nikzad’s intervention comes after the Iranian army vowed to respond to any new US attacks with “an immediate, crushing response”.
  
    



  



Earlier on Sunday, the Iranian army's spokesperson, Mohammad Akraminia, stressed that Iran’s war strategy has shifted from a “purely defensive stance to an offensive approach some time ago".

“Should a new war erupt, the geography of the conflict will not be confined to the West Asia region,” Akraminia told Iran state media. “Any potential future war could prove significantly longer than past conflicts.” 

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still had to "take care of" one or two targets.

"We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Trump said.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, however, said Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran, and that the US would be open to a diplomatic solution.

The United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, said it hoped for a breakthrough between Iran and the US while preparing for the worst.

"We're hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough," diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president Anwar Gargash said during a conference in Manama.

"It is not the interest of the region to go through another round... But I think we're also, as we've shown before, braced for the worst."

Following a visit to Tehran this week by a Qatari delegation, Iran has dispatched envoys to the Gulf country to continue consultations as part of indirect negotiations with the US to end the war.

Earlier this week, US Senator Chris Murphy described Trump's plan to restart the war on Iran as "insane" and said it would lead to a "devastating escalation".

"You've heard a preview that it would be a short-duration plan. I'll just say this: their plan is insane," Murphy said, speaking at an event organised by the Middle East Institute in Washington, DC.

"It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law."

Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, made the comments after American media reported that the US warned several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military offensive against Iran after the US midterm elections on 3 November.

“We have now reached a plan that cuts the implementation time to two days. On day one, the US implements a set of measures. On day two, the Hormuz Strait will reopen, and navigation will be restored to what it used to be.”

articles.title: Why is Syria considering joining the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact?
articles.description:
Why is Syria considering joining the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact?

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Reem Aouir
 on 
Mon, 11/02/2026 - 09:04

        
      
    
      
    
                Analyst says the move is a bargaining chip with Israel and doubts Syria will become the pact’s fourth member soon
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Syria's Foreign Minister Asaad Shaibani speaks during a plenary session of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) Manama Dialogue on 31 October 2026 (Fadhel Madan / AFP)
                  Off
                  Syria is considering joining the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday.

"Discussions are currently under way to evaluate Syria's entry into the Mecca alliance," al-Shaibani said during a session on regional security at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain.

He described Syria as an "integral" part of regional security and said Damascus would support any framework aimed at protecting stability across the region.

The Middle East was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems, he added. 

The comments mark a potential expansion of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan in Mecca on 7 August, to strengthen cooperation across their defence sectors.
  
    



  



As per the agreement, each signatory is committed to treating an attack on one member as an attack on all three, establishing a mutual defence arrangement similar in principle to Nato's collective security framework, which holds 32 member states.

During his speech in Bahrain, al-Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for Yemen's internationally recognised government in its efforts to restore sovereignty and stability across the country.

The foreign minister also called on regional actors to respect states' unity and sovereignty, while warning against actions that undermine regional stability.


Syria's foreign minister says Damascus is considering joining the Mecca alliance that binds Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in a Nato-style defence pact. https://t.co/8vP9tQnLdP
— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 1, 2026

The talks over Syria's joining the Mecca pact are in the early stages and Damascus is unlikely to become the pact’s fourth member in the near term, political analyst and senior advisor at Syria Report, Samy Akil, told Middle East Eye. 


“We’re still in the speculation phase, so nothing has been decided yet. But I do think it’s a bit of sabre-rattling by Syrian authorities,” Akil said.

“I don’t think at the current moment that Syria will necessarily be the fourth addition to the security pact. It will take some time, but the intent is there. It’s being tested. It will all come down, at the end of the day, to the fine print.”

The discussions come as Saudi Arabia faces an escalation in attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement, which has targeted airports, military installations and energy infrastructure across the kingdom.

Escalation in Saudi Arabia   

On Friday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had intercepted Houthi drones over the Mecca and Medina regions. The group later denied carrying out the attacks.

Akil said the timing of Shaibani’s remarks reflected Syria’s reading of the regional situation. 


'I think it is more related to the impending regional conflict that will likely witness a new round of escalation in the coming days'

- Samy Akil, Syria Report


“I think it is more related to the impending regional conflict that will likely witness a new round of escalation in the coming days. This is strategic thinking here, to do a bit of a balancing act,” he said.

Riyadh has been rallying international support, and the attacks have brought the agreement's military provisions into focus.

Both Pakistan and Turkey have pledged military support to the kingdom but have not announced any operations against the Houthis.

According to Al Jazeera, Turkish officials have ruled out sending troops to fight in Yemen, and the Turkish parliament’s foreign affairs committee has approved a bill to ratify the pact.

Syria has increasingly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia over the Houthi attacks, condemning strikes on airports and civilian infrastructure and supporting the kingdom's efforts to protect its security.

Saudi Arabia has emerged as one of the key regional partners of Syria's new government since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.
  
    



  



President Ahmed al-Sharaa visited Riyadh on 6 October, where he met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Their discussions focused on strengthening bilateral relations, reconstruction and investment, as well as regional developments.

After the visit, Damascus has denied all reports that Riyadh had asked it to deploy ground troops to Saudi Arabia to fight against the Houthis.

Ahmad Zaidan, a media adviser to al-Sharaa, said on X that the reports were “a lie and have no basis in truth”. The Syrian foreign ministry’s media department also said the country's regional policy was focused on stability, peace and co-operation, not opening new fronts.

Regional cooperation   

Syrian forces could be drawn into the conflict but argued that it would not be a wise decision, Akil said, adding that “fighting in Yemen differed from the type of warfare Syrian forces were used to.”

“Personally, I do think that Syria’s overall contribution at the end of the day will be something similar to what they contributed during Operation Desert Storm, meaning a small contingent of forces that will lay back and provide logistical support to Saudi forces, rather than be shock troops and troops on the ground,” he said.

Joining the Mecca agreement would nevertheless be a further step toward closer security cooperation between Damascus and Riyadh.

The foreign minister also criticised Israel's military operations in Syria, saying “our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, which have killed dozens.”


  

  Mecca alliance visits Tehran in push to end Israeli-US war and build regional security
    Read More »


"How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?" he asked.

Akil said Damascus's interest in the agreement could also be linked to its efforts to strengthen its position in future negotiations with Israel.

With Israeli forces continuing to occupy positions in southern Syria, he argued, Syrian authorities may see closer security ties with regional powers as a way to gain leverage.

He said Damascus was seeking to build a "bargaining chip" for future negotiations with Israel, particularly as an Israeli withdrawal from the south was unlikely in the short to medium term.

He added that membership would give Syria the right to activate the pact’s provisions should it come under attack.

In his Friday speech, al-Shaibani also renewed Syria’s demand for Israeli forces to pull back to their pre-8 December 2024 positions and for the 1974 disengagement agreement to be enforced.
  
    



  



For Damascus, closer security cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan could provide a framework for strengthening its regional partnerships.

But whether that would translate into concrete military commitments, and what role Syria could play in the agreement, remains unclear.

articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
articles.description:
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands

    
    

        
    
                Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to its conditions, as US President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for the upcoming US midterm elections.

A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told reporters at a briefing.

Reporting by AFP

articles.title: Sisi's 2030 exit plan would keep Egypt in the army's hands
articles.description:
Sisi's 2030 exit plan would keep Egypt in the army's hands

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Hesham Gaafar
 on 
Fri, 10/23/2026 - 20:00

        
      
    
      
    
                A proposed 30-month Military Academy course for future presidents would let the armed forces decide who is qualified to govern, sidelining parties and narrowing voters' choice
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, between then Defence Minister Mohamed Zaki (left) and Military Academy Director Ashraf Salem Zaher, who has since replaced Zaki, at the academy in Cairo on 30 May 2023 (Egyptian Presidency/AFP)
                  Off
                  At the Egyptian Military Academy's first graduation ceremony on 17 October, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said what many Egyptians had stopped expecting to hear. He declared that 2030 will mark the end of his presidency, "if I live", and that the matter is "completely settled".

Most coverage stopped there, but the consequential part of the speech came next, when Sisi proposed a 30-month programme of more than 7,500 hours at the academy for doctorate holders aged between 40 and 50, from whom Egyptians would later choose their presidents, ministers and governors.

The armed forces would pay "whatever it costs", and a committee including the speaker of parliament and the ministers of higher education and justice would draft a law setting out the selection criteria.

Together, the two halves of the speech describe a president deciding where power will reside after him, rather than returning it to Egyptians. The answer is the military.

Every personalised regime faces the same dilemma, since naming a successor creates a rival while naming no one leaves the elite to fight over the vacuum. Sisi is trying to sidestep both. The 2019 amendments allow him to appoint a vice president, the route Sadat and Mubarak used to reach power, yet he has never used it.
  
    



  



Instead, he is institutionalising the gate rather than the heir, so that whoever governs next would have to pass through an institution owned and financed by the army.

The academy has been moving towards this role for years, running mandatory courses for newly appointed imams, teachers, judges and diplomats. In September, Sisi called it "a gateway to employment in the Egyptian state".

The new proposal climbs the final rung, from training those who are appointed to training those who rule. The defence minister appointed in February, Ashraf Salem Zaher, ran the academy until the day he took office.

The army's veto

The second element, the veto, is already written into the constitution. Sisi read aloud Article 200, which charges the armed forces with safeguarding "the constitution and democracy" and "the civilian nature of the state", saying he had insisted on it in 2014. In fact, that wording came with the 2019 amendments that extended his own rule.

He then promised that no "malicious person, traitor or criminal" would take charge "according to the text I have just read", and added that "what I don't say is more than what I say".


Whoever governs next would have to pass through an institution owned and financed by the army


The result is a soft filter that manufactures a preferred elite and a hard veto that lets the army decide who counts as a threat. "We will not prevent anyone," Sisi said, and the door is formally open, but guarded.

None of this requires touching the constitution, because Article 141 leaves "other conditions" for presidential candidates to be defined by law.

Ordinary legislation can require a doctorate, a set age range and an academy certificate, so the promise that the constitution "will not be touched" can be honoured to the letter while the rules of access to power change entirely.

With 30 of the remaining 43 months needed for training, the law must pass in 2027, the very year rumours had assigned to an amendment extending his rule.

The trigger lies inside the regime rather than on the street. In November 2025, parliamentary elections meant to be a formality became an open contest among the state's own agencies.

According to Hossam el-Hamalawy, citing Mada Masr reporting, the interior ministry's security apparatus, which backed the Nation's Future Party, clashed with General Intelligence and Military Intelligence, which backed rival loyalist parties.

Sisi intervened publicly, and the election authority annulled the results in 19 districts, with the courts later voiding many more.

Why now, and what for

On 29 September, in a meeting with the cabinet, governors and the heads of the army and police, Sisi spoke of attempts to set "the interior ministry against the judiciary, the army against someone else, the agencies against each other", and urged officials to stop hiding their opinions.
  
    



  



Two weeks later he declared the constitution untouchable, and three days after that he announced 2030.

The lesson of 2025 is that the unity of Egypt's security apparatus rests on a single arbiter rather than on its structure. Once he announces his departure, every agency starts positioning itself. The academy proposal tries to hand that arbitration to the army before he leaves, though it may provoke the very rivalry it seeks to contain.


  

  Yemen war: Why Egypt's vow to defend Saudi Arabia is a risky gamble
    Read More »


Other pressures raised the cost of leaving succession open, including a campaign urging Sisi to rule until 2050 that revived talk of a presidency for life.

The IMF programme ends in December, while Egypt's financing needs are expected to stay high until close to 2030. A Saudi deposit worth more than $5bn fell due in October, and the war in Yemen has flared again, threatening Red Sea shipping.

In the same speech, Sisi pledged to defend Saudi Arabia "in accordance with the directives" of its rulers. For Gulf patrons and creditors, the message was that an army is available now and that Egypt will be predictable after 2030.

The deeper significance lies in what the proposal allows politics to be. For Sisi, the qualification to rule is knowing "what a state means", and no one who merely "says two well-arranged words" should imagine he can lead Egypt. In this view, politics is technical knowledge of the state, which only the state can certify.

The design leaves no role for parties, unions or social movements in producing leaders. In effect, the academy replaces parliament as the school of rulers, and legitimacy shifts from consent to competence certified by an institution issuing a diploma, rather than by voters judging performance.

A doctorate from a "reputable" university and 30 months of full-time training also form a class filter few dissidents, workers or provincial politicians could pass.

More than one way

One proposed exemption deserves particular attention. Sisi would exempt anyone with six years or more in government ministries, saying such experience qualifies them for "the responsibility of a state".

Since the programme cannot produce graduates before 2029, realistic candidates for 2030 are likely to come from this exempt pool of technocrats who owe Sisi their careers. The clause covers ministries but says nothing about the security agencies.

Such a successor would be weak by design, which may suit the military but also leaves room for the outgoing president.

The 2019 amendments bar more than two consecutive terms, not two in total; the transitional article granting Sisi his extra term is open to interpretation by a constitutional court whose president he selects; and if a successor resigns, elections follow within 90 days. None of this proves intent, but the pledge can be fulfilled in more than one way.



Sisi's record counsels caution, since he denied he would run in 2013 and then ran, and backed two four-year terms in 2017 before the 2019 amendments extended his rule. This pledge, though, is more specific than any before it, tied to a date, a committee, a budget and a timetable.

Parliamentary sources close to one of the security agencies told Mada Masr he does not want to repeat Mubarak's mistake of clinging to office. Reversing course would be costly, with a military now given a stake in the rules rather than the man.

The real test comes in 2027, not 2030, and it turns on who sits on the selection committee, whether the programme becomes a condition for candidacy, whether the exemption is widened to the security agencies and whether a vice president is finally appointed.

Egypt's presidents have seldom left office by choice. Sisi may choose to leave, but on terms that entrench, rather than end, the army's political role and replace representation with administration. The question for Egyptians is less whether he leaves in 2030 than whether anything he leaves behind will allow them to choose.

articles.title: Recognising Hamas as 'terror' outfit: Eisenkot lays down conditions for 'broad Zionist government'
articles.description:
Recognising Hamas as 'terror' outfit: Eisenkot lays down conditions for 'broad Zionist government'   

    
    

        
    
                Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has set out four conditions for forming a new government, including recognising Hamas as a "terrorist" organisation and committing to dismantle its military and governing capabilities in Gaza, as he seeks to use an opposition parliamentary majority to end Benjamin Netanyahu's rule.

In a statement posted on X on Saturday, the Yashar party leader said he was prepared to work with any elected lawmaker who accepted his principles for a broad "Zionist government".

These include recognising Israel as a "Jewish, democratic, liberal and egalitarian state", upholding the values of its Declaration of Independence, and introducing compulsory military or civilian national service for all citizens.

"The door to the government we will establish is open to every elected official who accepts these principles," he said, calling for an "extraordinary effort" to avoid another election and a prolonged political crisis.

Eisenkot vowed to move swiftly to use the new Knesset majority against what he called the "government of October 7", referring to the Netanyahu administration and its handling of the failures surrounding the Hamas-led attack on Israel in 2023.

He said a majority of Israeli voters, by more than half a million votes, had rejected the outgoing government and draft evasion in favour of political change. He pledged to introduce legislation establishing a state commission of enquiry into the 7 October failures, make national service compulsory for all Israelis and repeal the controversial judicial overhaul laws passed by the outgoing government.

The election, however, has produced a hung parliament, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. Anti-Netanyahu parties secured 67 seats, against 53 for the outgoing coalition, but the opposition total includes 48 seats held by Zionist parties and 19 won by the two Arab-led parties, the Joint List and Ra'am.

Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, while Eisenkot's Yashar finished second with 21. The opposition's numerical advantage therefore does not automatically translate into a governing majority, particularly given the reluctance of several Jewish opposition leaders to formally cooperate with Arab parties.שבוע טוב.
מספר דברים ממני אליכם, אחיי ואחיותיי הישראלים, לקראת הימים הקרובים: 

ספירת הקולות הסתיימה והבחירות נגמרו. בכל דרך בה מסתכלים על המספרים, רוב אזרחי ישראל, בהפרש של יותר מחצי מיליון קולות, הצביעו נגד ממשלת השבעה באוקטובר וההשתמטות, ובעד שינוי - רוב בקרב כלל אזרחי ישראל, ורוב בקרב הציבור הציוני המשרת. 

הגדרתי את הבחירות הללו בשנה האחרונה כגורליות ביותר בתולדות ישראל ותוצאותיהן ברורות, אף שיש מי שפועל להטיל בהן דופי. הבטחתי לחבר מחדש את ישראל ולשים סוף לתרבות השקר שהוביל נתניהו ופירקה אותנו מבפנים. הבטחתי שתחת הנהגתי, צד א׳ לא יכריע את צד ב׳, שתם עידן ״אנחנו״ ו״הם״. לאור הבטחות אלה אמשיך לפעול גם בשבועות הקרובים.

במקביל, בכוונתי לפעול למימוש הרוב הפרלמנטרי המובהק באופן מיידי, לטובת כלל אזרחי ישראל. לפעול להקמת ועדת חקירה ממלכתית, קידום חובת שירות לכל ופעולה מיידית להגדלה וחיזוק היקף המשרתים בצה"ל, תגמול והוקרה ראויה למשרתים, ביטול חוקי ההפיכה המשטרית ועוד. אל תתנו לאף אחד להטעות אתכם: במדינת ישראל הכנסת היא שנותנת את אמונה בממשלה, ולא להפך.

במהלך קמפיין הבחירות הצבתי מטרה להקים ממשלה ציונית ממלכתית עם הסכמה לאומית רחבה ככל האפשר שתביא לריפוי ושינוי יסודי בכיוון אליו ישראל הולכת.
הצבתי באופן עקבי 4 עקרונות שיחזקו את ישראל, לכל שותפות:
1.⁠ ⁠הכרה בישראל כמדינה יהודית, דמוקרטית, ליברלית ושוויונית.
2.⁠ ⁠מחויבות לערכי מגילת העצמאות.
3.⁠ ⁠חובת שירות לכלל אזרחי ישראל - צבאי, לאומי ואזרחי.
4.⁠ ⁠הכרה בחמאס כארגון טרור ובחובה להשמדת הכוח הצבאי-שלטוני שלו ברצועת עזה.

על בסיס עקרונות אלו, בכוונתי להקים ממשלה ציונית וממלכתית, רחבה ככל האפשר. לצורך כך אפעל בתיאום עם שותפיי ואפעל להרחיב את השותפות, על מנת לממש את רצון הבוחרים ולשפר באופן מיידי את מצבה הפנימי והבינלאומי של מדינת ישראל.

כל חבר כנסת שמוכן לחתום על עקרונות אלו, הוא שותף אפשרי בדרך לכינון ממשלה חדשה וטובה לישראל. דלת הממשלה שנקים תהייה פתוחה לכל נבחר ציבור שמקבל את עקרונות אלו ונכון להתעלות לגודל השעה.

ברור כי אחוזי ההצבעה הגבוהים, כמו גם האתגרים שעל הפרק, מחייבים מאמץ עילאי על מנת להימנע מבחירות נוספות וכניסה למשבר פוליטי מתמשך נוסף בכל דרך. ב-27.10 הציבור אמר את דברו וההחלטה על הרכבה של ממשלת ישראל הבאה היא של אזרחי ישראל בלבד, ללא מעורבות ומניפולציה - כך ראוי שיהיה. כעת מוטלת עלינו, נבחרי הציבור, החובה לעשות הכל על מנת לתרגם את רצון העם.

מחדל השבעה באוקטובר ובהמשכו המציאות הביטחונית, הפנימית, הכלכלית והבינלאומית מחייבים החלטות אמיצות ובהקדם. אפעל בכל דרך להביא הסכמה לאומית רחבה ככל האפשר על מנת שנוכל להתחיל בתיקון ושיקום.

לסיום, המלחמה נגד אויבינו לא תמה. מטרות המלחמה לא הושגו. עד להקמת הממשלה אתן גיבוי למהלכים צבאיים רק במידה ויהיו איומים ישירים ומיידיים כנגד ישראל שלא יכולים להמתין עד להשבעת הממשלה.

לא נשלה את עצמנו. אנו בפני שבועות עמוסים, מורכבים ועתירי ספינים ושקרים. 
בכוונתי לפעול באומץ ומתוך מחויבות גדולה לבוחר ולמדינה על מנת לממש את רצונו - בשקט וביצירתיות.

נעשה ונצליח, למען כולנו ולמען מדינת ישראל. אני מתחייב.— Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) October 31, 2026

“The despicable and malicious attempt to deny the election results, undermine the will of the public, smear an entire community, and drag Israel into another round of elections has failed,” Eisenkot wrote in Hebrew on X.

articles.title: Aipac is now a toxic brand. The Michigan Senate race is only one example
articles.description:
Aipac is now a toxic brand. The Michigan Senate race is only one example

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Mitchell Plitnick
 on 
Wed, 10/28/2026 - 15:28

        
      
    
      
    
                The pro-Israel lobbying group has worked tirelessly to portray an apartheid regime that is committing genocide as a warm and friendly country - US voters have finally wised up 

                      
                  
                  

  


                  Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks to supporters on 1 November 2026 in Michigan (AFP)
                  Off
                  “A lobby is like a night flower: it thrives in the dark and dies in the sun.” So said Steve Rosen, former foreign policy director of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) in a memo to a fellow staffer. Rosen would later be fired amid a major scandal involving espionage in passing classified US information to Israel. 

Rosen was correct about the danger to a lobbying organisation that publicity poses. But in December 2021, Aipac decided to test that theory by creating two political action committees (Pacs) that enabled it to take part directly in political campaigns.

The results were mixed, and Aipac recently announced that it was closing one of the Pacs it had set up. 

Aipac had been an advocacy organisation, promoting Israel’s interests, but it did not fund campaigns directly, nor did it endorse or fund political candidates. 

In many ways, that made it more effective. It could do things like issue a congressional report card which rated every member of Congress’s support of Israel. Then other groups that were actual Pacs could use those reports to decide which candidates they should be contributing to. 
  
    



  



Aipac’s non-profit status allows it to lobby Congress on behalf of Israel while claiming it acts strictly in support of the wishes of pro-Israel Americans. It thus avoids having to register as an agent of a foreign government. 

Meanwhile, Aipac’s sister organisation, the American Israel Education Fund, which is registered as an education non-profit, refrains from direct lobbying but offers vacation tours to Israel for members of Congress, under the rubric of “education”.

This strategy was effective for decades. Aipac’s bipartisan reach was strong, and it was often remarked by a credulous media how Israel was, somehow, the one subject Democrats and Republicans could come together on.

Changing opinion

That began to change in recent years.

    Read More »

Aipac works tirelessly to portray an apartheid regime that is committing genocide as a warm, friendly country. Like a lobby, that effort cannot withstand the sunlight, and even Aipac’s own officials know it.

                Israel, the only country to recognise breakaway Somali territory, continues to strengthen its ties
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Israel's ambassador to Somaliland, Michael Lotem (L) receives his credentials from Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (Republic of Somaliland via social media)
                  Off
                  Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland presented his credentials to the breakaway territory’s president last week, according to a statement issued by the Israeli foreign ministry on Sunday. 

Israel is the only state in the world to have recognised Somaliland, which also enjoys substantial economic ties to the United Arab Emirates.

Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi formally accepted Michael Lotem’s credentials at a ceremony in Hargeisa, Somaliland’s capital, while officials also laid the cornerstone for an Israeli embassy.

Israel’s foreign ministry said the ceremony marked “another important step in strengthening relations between Israel and Somaliland, following their mutual recognition on 26 December 2025”.

Since Israel recognised Somaliland, an autonomous region in northern Somalia that declared independence in 1991, ties between the countries have continued to develop. 
  
    



  



Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar has visited Somaliland, while Somaliland opened an embassy in west Jerusalem during a visit made by Abdullahi in June.

“Israel is determined to develop and strengthen its relations with Somaliland,” Saar said after the presentation of credentials.

Abdullahi said during the ceremony that it was the first time a Somaliland president had received the credentials of an ambassador from a UN member state recognising its independence.

Ambassador Lotem said Israel’s recognition acknowledged what Somaliland had built over 35 years, rather than serving as a mere diplomatic formality.

Strategic Somaliland

Somaliland and Israel are in talks about the possibility of Israel building a naval base on Somaliland’s Red Sea coast, which sits close to the strategically vital Bab al-Mandab strait.


  

  Inside Somaliland: How Berbera Port is central to the Red Sea's power struggle
    Read More »


At the ceremony in Hargeisa, Abdullahi emphasised the relevance of Somaliland’s geography.

“Given our strategic position around the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, our cooperation also carries important regional and international significance,” he said.
 
“Let me reaffirm that Somaliland approaches this relationship with genuine strategic commitment and a long-term perspective.”

Berbera, the commercial capital of Somaliland, is at the heart of this strategic importance. 

DP World, the Emirati logistics company, runs the main port there, as part of a partnership with the British government’s foreign investment arm.

The UAE also has a military base at Berbera.

                  US Democrat Haley Stevens has said she is endorsing Republican candidate Mike Rogers, over her own party's nominee Abdul El-Sayed, days before the Michigan Senate contest.

Aipac-backed Stevens, who lost the Michigan Senate primary to progressive El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival in a video posted on X on Sunday, just days before the midterm elections.

The race is considered by analysts to be one of the most important Senate contests of the cycle.

El-Sayed is an outspoken critic of Israel's genocide in Gaza, whereas Rogers is a hardline Republican ally of US President Donald Trump.

The move prompted a fierce backlash among Democrats, with Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, condemning it as a "despicable betrayal".
  
    



  



El-Sayed himself refused to be drawn into the backlash, saying "none of this matters".

“I don’t want any distractions,” he said, according to the New York Times.

"Folks are more interested in making this race about things that it’s not about.”

In the video, which she posted shortly after a surprise appearance alongside Rogers at a church in Detroit, Stevens said that she doesn't "belong in Abdul's campaign".

"Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now," she added.


    Aipac and the Michigan Senate race: How the Israel lobby became toxic

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters as she stood alongside Rogers outside the church.

"We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum, and will not allow these eleventh-hour distractions deter us.”

                The World Travel Market event is set to begin on Tuesday and advertise the Jerusalem Development Authority
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Britain's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband attends the meeting of the top diplomats in Istanbul on 23 October 2026 (AFP)
                  Off
                  Fifteen MPs have written to the British government demanding "urgent action" to stop an international travel event in London, set to begin on Tuesday, from advertising an Israeli agency involved in the construction of illegal settlements.

MEE revealed last week that the World Travel Market (WTM) event, which is scheduled to take place in London between 3-5 November, will feature a stand run by the Israeli government's tourist office.

The Israeli stand is shared by numerous Israeli companies and organisations, including "iTravelJerusalem", which promotes tourism in Israeli-occupied East Jerusalem and is managed by the Jerusalem Development Authority (JDA).

The JDA, a statutory agency of the Israeli government and the Jerusalem municipality, carries out development initiatives across Jerusalem and has been heavily involved in the construction and expansion of illegal Israeli settlements on occupied Palestinian territory.

Independent MP Adnan Hussain sent a letter to Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Monday, which was signed by MPs from multiple parties, including Labour MPs John McDonnell and Kim Johnson, and former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn.
  
    



  



The letter, seen by MEE, demands that the government "contact the organisers of WTM London and require the removal of exhibitors and promotional material where their participation would facilitate or promote illegal Israeli settlements".

It asks the government to confirm "what steps are being taken to ensure that the ban on the advertising of illegal settlements is enforced in practice, rather than being confined to statements made in Parliament".

Last month, the British government recognised Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory as illegal and announced comprehensive sanctions on Israeli settlements.

All five Green Party MPs - Carla Denyer, Ellie Chownes, Hannah Spencer, Sian Berry and Adrian Ramsay - signed the letter, as did independent MPs Shockat Adam, Iqbal Mohamed and Ayoub Khan, as well as Scottish National Party MP Chris Law.

The letter says: "The Government cannot credibly condemn the forced displacement of Palestinians, identify ethnic cleansing in the occupied Palestinian territory, and commit to prohibiting the promotion of illegal settlements in the United Kingdom, while allowing organisations implicated in these activities to use a major international event in London to promote their work."

'We expect an urgent response'

According to a 2025 report by the Office of the European Union Representative for the West Bank and Gaza Strip, the JDA planned "for the eviction of the Umm Haroun compound - home to approximately 40 Palestinian families - and the construction of a 320-unit settlement" in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood. 


  

  Exclusive: London event advertises Israeli agency building illegal settlements
    Read More »


In 2020, a JDA project to build a cable car in Jerusalem, which would involve the uprooting of trees and displacement of infrastructure including water, sewage and telecommunications, was approved by the Israeli government.

The JDA also plans to build a large settlement housing project next to the Palestinian community of Beit Safafa in East Jerusalem.

Hussam Zomlot, the Palestinian ambassador to Britain, said in response to MEE's report last Thursday: "Next week Israeli companies guilty of ethnic cleansing will be platformed at [WTM London]."

Zomlot added: "The UK government must now turn their words into action: enforce these commitments and ensure those complicit in illegal occupation and settlements face real consequences."

Hussain's letter sent on Monday says: "We expect an urgent response setting out the specific steps you will take before the event opens. A response limited to restating the Government’s position will not suffice.

"The question is no longer simply what the Government believes, but whether it is prepared to act on what it has said."

MEE reached out to WTM and the Foreign Office for comment but did not receive a response by time of publication.

                  Off
                  Britain's governing Labour Party has decided to stop cooperating with the Green Party in 11 councils across England over the Greens adopting a policy that "Zionism is racism" last month.

Bridget Phillipson, the Labour chair, said the Green motion on Zionism "crosses a line and we cannot work with any party that supports it - at any level of government".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham denounced the motion as "antisemitic" last month. The Green Party said it would "not take lectures" from a government that supplies weapons to Israel. 

According to Labour, cooperation with the Greens will stop on Arun, Derbyshire Dales, Havant, Lewes, Sheffield, Stafford, Warwick, Wealden, West Devon and West Suffolk councils.

Six Green council groups, in Broadland, Monmouthshire, North Somerset, Rother, West Oxfordshire and West Sussex, have condemned the motion.
  
    



  



Phillipson said: "Any local power-sharing arrangement cannot come at the expense of upholding the moral obligation we have to stand up for everyone in our communities and the values we share.

"We are pleased that some local Green parties have rightly opted to disavow this policy and have called on their party’s leadership to do the same. It is disappointing that some local Green parties have not met the conditions Labour has set out.

"Labour continues to oppose this divisive policy and calls on the Green party to do the right thing and rescind it."

"Leaders across these parties are rightly proud of what those partnerships have achieved.

                  Off
                  Michigan's Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has sparked controversy after endorsing Republican Mike Rogers in the state's Senate race, less than 48 hours before Election Day, despite repeatedly assuring fellow Democrats she would support her former primary rival, Abdul El-Sayed.

The abrupt reversal, coming roughly 12 hours after her reported assurances, has prompted widespread criticism from Democratic lawmakers and political commentators, with particular attention focused on Stevens' subsequent attempts to explain her decision.

During a tense interview with CNN's Anderson Cooper on Sunday, Stevens was repeatedly pressed to explain what had changed overnight.

"Well, look, this is just a weight off my shoulders, OK?" Stevens responded, before accusing Sayed of becoming increasingly angry and making some Democrats feel unwelcome in his campaign.
  
    



  



"Nothing with me changed, Anderson," she insisted.

Cooper challenged the explanation, noting that Stevens had previously described Rogers as a potential rubber stamp for President Donald Trump's agenda and warned against giving Republicans another Senate seat.

As Stevens continued to discuss her disagreements with Sayed without identifying a specific turning point, Cooper expressed frustration.

"You're not really answering any of my questions, so it's somewhat frustrating," he said.

The exchange quickly drew widespread online criticism, with numerous commentators questioning how Stevens could claim nothing had changed while reversing her endorsement within hours.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticised Stevens for betraying the working class  “by endorsing the very Republican she said she wanted to run against”.


Working class people’s lives are on the ballot on Tuesday—their healthcare, their rent, their bills. Haley Stevens just betrayed them by endorsing the very Republican she said she wanted to run against.
— Zohran Kwame Mamdani (@ZohranKMamdani) November 1, 2026


Stevens cites Hasan Piker and antisemitism

Stevens defended her endorsement by pointing to Sayed's association with progressive streamer Hasan Piker, and disagreements over antisemitism.

"We can't stand with hate. We can't stand with Hasan Piker," Stevens said while appearing alongside Rogers.
  
    



  



During her CNN interview, she again invoked Piker and his uncle, political commentator Cenk Uygur, as reasons for her decision.

However, Cooper pointed out that these associations were already known when Stevens initially endorsed Sayed, raising further questions about why her position had changed so suddenly.

Stevens also cited an advertisement by an outside political group that linked the cost of living in Michigan to US financial support for Israel. The advertisement was criticised for invoking antisemitic tropes, although Sayed had publicly disagreed with its framing, according to Axios.

Her explanation prompted another wave of online criticism, with commentators questioning the timing of her objections and the consistency of her decision to support Rogers.

— Hasanabi Productions (fan account) (@HasanabiProd) November 2, 2026


Jewish Democratic leaders challenge Stevens

Stevens' attempt to frame her endorsement around concerns about antisemitism also drew criticism from the leadership of the Democratic National Committee's Jewish-American Council.

In a joint statement shared on X, council chair Adam Goldwyn and vice chair Steph Newton acknowledged disagreements with Sayed over Israel and Jewish safety but warned against using those concerns for political purposes.

"Those disagreements deserve to have serious discussion, not political exploitation," they said.

The leaders also accused Stevens of overlooking antisemitism controversies involving Rogers' campaign, citing students associated with his outreach operation who had defended a Young Republicans group chat containing praise for Adolf Hitler.
  
    



  



"If Stevens actually cared about protecting Jews, she would have raised those concerns with Rogers' campaign before endorsing the MAGA Republican. She did not," the statement read.

The council leaders went on to criticise Rogers' alignment with Trump and urged Michigan voters to support Sayed.

Their statement added to criticism from other Jewish Democrats who have rejected Stevens' endorsement despite expressing their own concerns about Sayed's rhetoric and political associations.

According to The Times of Israel, Michigan congressional candidate Jeremy Moss, who has publicly disagreed with Sayed, also rejected Rogers as an alternative. "Mike Rogers is not the solution to this problem," Moss said.

Representative Jamie Raskin, who reportedly spoke with Stevens on Saturday night, expressed disbelief at her reversal, while Michigan's Congresswoman Debbie Dingell questioned the timing of the decision.

Sayed, meanwhile, has sought to move past the controversy, telling reporters on Sunday that he was focused on Michigan voters rather than Stevens.

Houthis launched cross border raids on Saudi military posts, sources say
articles.description:
Houthis launched cross border raids on Saudi military posts, sources say

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Sean Mathews
 on 
Mon, 11/02/2026 - 17:37

        
      
    
      
    
                Houthi incursion into Saudi Arabia took place as recently as late October
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Supporters of the Houthi authorities shout slogans during a protest against the Saudi intervention in Yemen and against Saudi Arabia's recent accusation that the Houthis fired at the holy city of Mecca, in Sanaa, on 18 September 2026 (Mohammed Huwais/AFP)
                  Off
                  The Houthis have launched multiple cross-border raids into Saudi Arabia in recent months, in an expansion of the conflict beyond Yemen, a western and Arab official with direct knowledge of the raids told Middle East Eye.

The small-scale raids have targeted border posts in Saudi Arabia’s rugged, mountainous southwest. At least one raid occurred at the end of October, the officials told MEE.

The western official told MEE that the Houthis, officially known as Ansar Allah, appear to have captured specific small arms that are known only to be used by Saudi border security forces.

The end-of-October cross-border raid was also observed on surveillance equipment, the official added.

The raids, which have not been publicly reported, would mark the first instance of Houthi cross-border attacks inside Saudi Arabia since the collapse of a ceasefire in Yemen.
  
    



  



Before the 2022 truce was signed, Saudi Arabia reported regular attempts by the Houthis to infiltrate the kingdom, as the Houthis conducted ground raids on border cities and army bases.

Mohammed al-Basha, a Yemen expert and founder of the Basha Report Risk Advisory, told MEE he was closely watching Houthi military activity at the Saudi border, where the group is “gradually expanding the range and intensity” of attacks.

“The initial phase involved long-range drones and short-range ballistic missiles. The second phase introduced short-range quadcopters that drop mortar munitions, as well as sniper operations,” he said.

Basha said it was “only a matter of time” before the Houthis returned to launching ground raids.

“I expect the initial operations to resemble the early years of the nearly 12-year Yemen war, when the Houthi fighters carried out hit-and-run attacks, captured coalition personnel, seized weapons and destroyed military equipment and vehicles before withdrawing,” added Basha, who is an associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute. 

The Arab official told MEE that Egyptian, Pakistani and Turkish military assistance would likely be valuable along the kingdom’s southern border as a result of the raids. 

Saudi Arabia’s Mecca Pact allies, Turkey and Pakistan, have said they plan to deploy forces, including air defence batteries, to the kingdom. Egypt’s parliament also approved the deployment of defensive forces to Saudi Arabia last week.
  
    



  



Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that Damascus is also thinking of joining the pact. The western official told MEE that some Syrian drone specialists had already arrived in Yemen to assist the Saudi-backed forces.

Houthi claims on southern Saudi Arabia

The Houthis’ cross-border attacks are unlikely to alter the military balance of power in Yemen, where Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces are struggling to stem a Houthi offensive. 

Reuters reported on Monday that the Houthis have advanced to within 50 miles of Aden port, which is the capital of the internationally recognised government. The group has also encircled Taiz. 


  

  Houthi strikes mark the end of Saudi Arabia's Yemen 'containment strategy'
    Read More »


The Houthis have launched hundreds of high-profile strikes on Saudi civilian infrastructure, including airports and energy installations. At least 24 people have been killed by the Houthi strikes. As a result, Riyadh was forced to cancel a high-profile investment forum.

But the cross-border raids have underscored the vulnerability of Saudi Arabia’s remote southern border and the difficulties of policing the vast terrain.

The attacks also reaffirm apprehension inside the kingdom that the Houthis have territorial ambitions. 

While the Houthis have mainly fought inside Yemen, they have revisionist claims against Saudi Arabia, particularly against its three southern provinces of Asir, Jazan and Najran, which Yemen ceded to Saudi Arabia in the 1934 Treaty of Taif.

The Houthis originated in Yemen’s Saada governorate, the mountainous region south of the border with Saudi Arabia.

The movement takes its name from its founder, Hussein Badreddin al-Houthi and follows the Zaydi sect of Shia Islam. The Houthis recruit across Yemeni society, but their senior leadership claims Hashemite descent, which would link them to the Prophet Muhammad.

articles.title: Hamas considered 'cancelling 7 October' attack if Israel honoured agreements
articles.description:
Hamas considered 'cancelling 7 October' attack if Israel honoured agreements

                Al Jazeera’s investigation reveals secret documents detailing objectives and the conditions Hamas set for abandoning the operation
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Fighters of the Ezzedine al-Qassam Brigades, Hamas's armed wing, attend the funeral of two fighters in Gaza City on 24 January 2025 (Omar al-Qattaa/AFP)
                  Off
                  Hamas’ plan for the 7 October 2023 attack reportedly included a clause allowing it to be cancelled if Israel honoured previous understandings with the Palestinian group, according to an Al Jazeera investigation.

The investigation, broadcast on Friday by the television programme The Hidden is Greater, revealed meeting records from the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, Hamas’ armed wing, in the months before the attack.

A meeting on 11 February 2023 discussed the operation, codenamed "Project Fahd". It stated that the plan would be abandoned “if the [Israeli] attacks on Al-Aqsa Mosque and in the prisons ceased”.

Yahya Sinwar, Hamas’ leader in Gaza at the time, and Mohammed Deif, head of its armed wing, reportedly attended the meeting. Both were killed by Israeli forces in 2024.

The document said the decision to pursue the operation came amid what it described as Israeli violations.
  
    



  



“The brutality at Al-Aqsa has reached unacceptable levels, and the same applies to the treatment of prisoners,” it stated.

On the political front, it said there were “no signs of progress”, accusing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of having “backtracked on everything previously agreed”.

“The operational objective of the project is to defeat the enemy’s Gaza Division,” another clause stated. The division is responsible for Israeli military operations along the Gaza border.

The document also identified the capture of as many Israeli soldiers as possible as an objective.

Middle East Eye could not independently verify the contents of the document.

Around 1,200 Israelis were killed during the Hamas-led assault on southern Israel. A further 251 people were taken captive.

Israel responded by launching its genocidal war on Gaza, killing at least 73,000 Palestinians over two years.
  
    



  



A US-brokered ceasefire in 2025 was intended to end the genocide, ease Israel’s siege and facilitate the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza.

However, Israel has continued to violate the agreement, carrying out near-daily attacks and demolitions of homes, and expanding its occupation of territory in the strip, forcing the population into less than half of Gaza. At least 1,500 people have been killed since the ceasefire took effect.

Israel has also largely maintained sweeping restrictions on aid deliveries, keeping essential food, medicine and shelter supplies out of reach.

Deif’s life and military leadership

The Al Jazeera investigation also revealed rare, previously unseen footage, recordings and documents detailing Deif’s early life and clandestine leadership of Hamas’ armed wing.

The footage included Deif attending a meeting in a tunnel with the group’s military leadership, including several commanders who have since been killed.



Other footage showed him visiting a rocket-manufacturing facility and military operations rooms.

Before the 7 October attack, no publicly available images of Deif were known, and little was known about his health following seven Israeli assassination attempts over the years.

Deif led Hamas’ armed wing from 2002 until he died in an Israeli air strike in July 2024. During his tenure, he oversaw the transformation of the al-Qassam Brigades from a guerrilla force into a quasi-military organisation with an estimated 30,000 fighters.

articles.description:
‘Our bombs killed hostages’ in Gaza, says former Israeli army chief

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by

                Approximately 87 died in captivity in Gaza or were taken there after having already died
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Herzi Halevi during a situational assessment in the Rafah area in the southern Gaza Strip on 14 August 2024 (Israeli Army via AFP)
                  Off
                  Israel’s former military chief has acknowledged that Israeli air strikes killed captives held by Palestinian groups in Gaza.

Speaking at a conference organised by the Shurat Hadin group in New York on Sunday, Herzi Halevi claimed military “pressure” on Gaza helped secure the release of captives.

But he admitted that Israeli forces had also killed some of them. “Our bombs killed hostages. We did not know they were there,” he said.

A total of 251 people were taken captive during the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023.

Most were later returned alive through prisoner exchanges with Hamas. Approximately 87 died in captivity in Gaza or were taken there after having already died.  
  
    



  



Israeli authorities have previously declined to address accusations that military strikes killed captives, instead accusing Hamas of killing them.

Israeli newspaper Maariv reported in October 2025, citing Israeli officials, that many captives had been killed by Israeli strikes, particularly during the early stages of the war.


  

  What is the Hannibal Directive and why is it controversial?
    Read More »


On 7 October, the Israeli military invoked the Hannibal Directive, a controversial order designed to prevent the capture of Israeli soldiers, even at the risk of killing them.

According to Israeli media reports, the military applied the directive along the Gaza-Israel boundary during the first hours of the Hamas-led assault.

Halevi, who resigned as military chief last year, also admitted on Sunday that the 7 October attack “was a failure that could have been prevented”.

However, he rejected suggestions that the assault resulted from internal betrayal.

“Helping Hamas would require not just one person collaborating, but a very broad network. After three years, not even one such person has been found,” he said.

articles.title: Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says
articles.description:
Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says

    
    

        
    
                Former Mossad chief David Barnea has said Israel intentionally released images of their covert operation in Iran during the June 2025 conflict to provoke mass arrests and make it harder for Iranian forces to find real Israeli agents.

“One of the reasons we immediately released an official video on the morning of Operation Rising Lion, with the Mossad logo, was to protect the agents who were there,” Barnea said, according to comments The Jerusalem Post reported on 25 October.

Barnea said the leak of the footage of Israeli operations in Iran was not just an attempt to showcase the Mossad’s reach but also a strategy to overwhelm Iranian counterintelligence, causing them to make mass arrests, making it more difficult to distinguish operatives from ordinary citizens.

“We wanted to make sure they arrested so many people in Iran that they wouldn’t be able to distinguish the wheat from the chaff and would eventually release everyone,” he said.

Barnea said Iranian authorities arrested 21,000 people during the operation.

“Some of the people being hanged in Iran on accusations of being Mossad agents, I have to ask who they are,” he said. “They tell me, ‘Listen, we don’t know either.’”

He described some of those executed as “just unfortunate people whom they decided were our agents, but who never worked for the Mossad, and probably never worked for any other intelligence organisation either”, according to the reported remarks.

The remarks made at the Priority Summit on 22 October to a private audience have sparked a sharp response from Trita Parsi.

Parsi, executive vice-president of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, described it as an admission that Israel "used ordinary Iranians as tools to protect Mossad operatives" in the country.

“Rarely will you find a more crude admission of how Israel deliberately and carelessly put thousands of people it claimed it sought to liberate in harm’s way,” Parsi wrote on X.

Mass detentions

Israel launched Operation Rising Lion on 13 June 2025, during which they bombed Iran and killed senior military commanders as well as scientists.

After Iran retaliated with missile attacks on Israel, the 12-day war ended with a ceasefire.

On the first morning of the attacks, the Mossad released videos showing what it said were its agents operating inside Iran.

The footage included attacks on ballistic missile and air-defence targets, with the faces of those involved concealed.

Iranian police announced in August 2025 that they had detained about 21,000 people during the 12-day conflict.

Police spokesperson Saeed Montazer al-Mahdi said the arrests followed reports from members of the public and increased security measures.

More than 260 suspects were arrested on suspicion of espionage and 172 people were arrested for illegal filming, the police statement said.

Barnea’s comments come amid concerns over Iran’s use of espionage allegations to prosecute people following the conflict.

Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch said in September 2025 that Iranian authorities had arrested more than 20,000 people after the outbreak of hostilities with Israel.

Those targeted included journalists, human rights activists, social media users, members of ethnic and religious minorities, and foreigners.

Iranian authorities have said they were responding to genuine threats from Israeli intelligence and collaborators inside the country.

Tehran has repeatedly accused the Mossad of recruiting people to gather intelligence, carry out sabotage and assist military attacks.

articles.title: Iran designates Britain's Royal Navy, RAF as 'terrorist' groups, report says
articles.description:
Iran designates Britain's Royal Navy, RAF as 'terrorist' groups, report says

    
    

        
    
                Iran's Foreign Ministry on Sunday designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist" organisations, in retaliation for what it described as hostile actions by the British government, including its designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a "terrorist organisation".

The ministry also designated Britain's foreign intelligence service, MI6, a "hostile group", saying the measures took effect on 1 November, according to Iran's Mehr News Agency.

The decision was taken under a resolution by Iran's Supreme National Security Council and followed Britain's designation of the IRGC under the State Threats Act 2026 on 13 July, the ministry said in a statement, Mehr reported.

Tehran also accused Britain of participating in the US-Israeli war against Iran by providing access to military and logistical bases and facilities under British jurisdiction.

The ministry said the measures were based on the principle of reciprocity and in accordance with international law, adding that the British government would be responsible for any consequences.

According to Mehr, the ministry condemned "Britain's anti-Iranian policies", saying they violated the principles of the United Nations Charter, including respect for national sovereignty and the prohibition of unlawful measures against other states. 

  
  
      



    Members of the US Air Force prepare munitions at RAF Fairford in south-west England on 10 March 2026. (AFP)

                The posters used an infamous but authentic photograph of a man in military uniform jeering at a Palestinian woman in the occupied West Bank
                      
                  
                  

  


                  L'Espresso's image edited and depicting the Israeli settler threatening Palestinians in the occupied West Bank (L'Espresso/Pietro Masturzo)

                  Off
                  London police have arrested a man over posters depicting an armed Israeli settler jeering at a Palestinian woman in the occupied West Bank after a complaint into its allegedly antisemitic connotations.

The posters, which carried the caption “Labour’s monsters”, showed an armed man in military uniform taunting a Palestinian woman.

Italian photojournalist Pietro Masturzo took the photograph in the occupied Palestinian village of Idhna, west of Hebron, on 12 October 2025 - the first day of the olive harvest.

Masturzo’s photograph appeared in the April edition of L’Espresso, alongside reports on the expansion of Israel’s settler movement and its impact on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

“The settler's expression is reflected in the gesture he repeats, mimicking the sound a shepherd makes when gathering his flock, addressing the Palestinians as if they were his own animals,” the photojournalist said.
  
    



  



The magazine also reported testimonies from Palestinians in the Jordan Valley, where settlers, often backed by Israeli forces, carry out near-daily attacks.

Police investigated the posters, which appeared around London during local elections in May. They were put up in protest at Labour’s support for Israel during the Gaza genocide.

'Stirs up hatred against Jewish people '

The investigation was triggered after a complaint filed to the police. According to The Daily Telegraph, the complaint described the image as a “monstrous characterisation” of a Jewish man.

The complainant also said the photograph was “selected to appear menacing”.

  
  
      



    L'Espresso's front page depicting an armed Israeli taunting Palestinians in the occupied West Bank (Screenshot from Instagram/Pietro Masturzo)
  





The unidentified complainant also claimed that the image was “anchored specifically in Jewish religious identity markers, not Israeli military conduct generally. This stirs up hatred against Jewish people.”

According to the complaint, the posters appeared to “frame the Labour Party as acting in the service of Israeli government policy” and that “Labour are complicit in genocide”.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “On Thursday, Oct 1, a 36-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of a racially aggravated public order offence following an incident in May, 2026, in which a number of anti-Semitic posters were displayed across Tower Hamlets. He was released on bail pending further inquiries.”

In September, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described attacks by Jewish settlers as “terrorism” supported by the Israeli state and said settlers were responsible for ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

articles.title: Al Jazeera celebrates 30 years 'of transforming news in Middle East and beyond'
articles.description:
Al Jazeera celebrates 30 years 'of transforming news in Middle East and beyond'

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff

                Qatari network announces 'new ecosystem' of news channels as it marks its 30th anniversary
                      
                  
                  

  


                  This picture taken on 11 August 2025 shows the headquarters of the news television network Al Jazeera in Doha, Qatar (AFP)
                  Off
                  Al Jazeera celebrated 30 years “of transforming news in Middle East and beyond” on Sunday, as the Qatari media network marked its anniversary and announced the launch of a new “ecosystem” of channels.

At a celebration in Doha, which was attended by the emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and senior network officials, Al Jazeera's message was that it “remains committed to telling stories to our global audiences with impartiality, truth and accuracy”.

Al Jazeera Arabic was launched 30 years ago, on 1 November 1996, with an initial grant of about $137m from the Qatari state and a recurring annual grant of about $100m. At first, the channel broadcast for just six hours a day.

The news channel, which, as the Guardian later reported, enjoyed “an unusual degree of editorial freedom, allowed by the Qatari government”, quickly “picked up Arab viewers disenchanted with state-controlled media in their own countries”.  

“Most analysts agree that Al Jazeera was, and is, a diplomatic exercise by the rich and savvy ruler of a small and geopolitically vulnerable nation,” former staff member Scott Bridges, now a media academic in Australia, wrote in 2012.
  
    



  



“But from the moment it was launched, this news network was a radical departure from the kind of state-owned television that is standard across the Middle East.”

Many of Al Jazeera Arabic’s initial staff were recruited from the BBC, which launched an Arabic TV channel a couple of years before the Qatari network, but then closed it down after censorship attempts from Saudi Arabia, which controlled the relevant satellite.

Al Jazeera Arabic’s popularity and acclaim grew during the US-led invasion of Afghanistan, when the network maintained the only 24-hour satellite link to Kabul and its footage was used by western channels.

Al Jazeera Arabic was followed 10 years later by the channel that is now known as Al Jazeera English, which was started with an initial investment of $1bn.

The Qatari network has been hailed for its coverage of the invasion of Iraq, the Syrian civil war, the Arab Spring revolutions and Israel’s genocide in Gaza, where at least 10 of its full-time staff and nine freelancers have been killed.

Last week, a Tel Aviv court approved a further 90-day extension of Israel’s closure of Al Jazeera’s office and ban on its operations in the country.

Israel first banned the network in May 2024 under a law targeting foreign broadcasters accused of being a “threat to national security”. Israeli forces also raided and closed Al Jazeera's Ramallah office in the occupied West Bank that September.
  
    



  



'New ecosystem of news channels'

At the event commemorating the 30th anniversary in Doha, Hamad bin Thamer bin Mohammed Al Thani, Al Jazeera’s chairman, said that his network had “achieved what we didn’t expect it to achieve in a short period of time, if we compare it to other international news organisations”.

Al Jazeera’s director general, Nasser bin Faisal bin Khalifa Al Thani, said that “pride in history, no matter how great, is not enough. Al Jazeera, which started a bold idea, cannot remain faithful to that beginning unless it has the courage of renewal”.

    Read More »


In a statement, Al Jazeera Media Network said it would be launching a “new ecosystem of news channels” under the slogan “Now. Meaning. Humanity.”

“The launch forms part of a strategic transformation in response to rapid changes in how audiences consume news and media,” the statement said. 

“It will give viewers a comprehensive perspective built on three pillars: speed and keeping pace with events (Now), depth and analysis (Meaning), and the human dimension (Humanity).”

In practice, this will centre on three channels. Al Jazeera Now, which will focus on “continuous coverage of major developing stories and escalating situations”, while Al Jazeera Arabic will deepen its news and investigatory coverage.

Al Jazeera Mubasher “will retain its identity as a channel that brings viewers events as they happen, providing a live, unmediated window onto the news directly from the field”, according to the statement.

Raed Fakih, Al Jazeera's director of news, said: “For three decades, Al Jazeera has helped transform the way news is covered in the Arab world, making room on screen for voices, issues and perspectives that had not been given the space they deserved.

“Today, as we mark Al Jazeera’s 30th anniversary, we are building on that editorial legacy to broaden the scope of our coverage and give greater prominence to a wider range of events and viewpoints.”

articles.title: Yemen’s foreign minister demands accountability for UN worker’s death in Houthi custody
articles.description:
Yemen’s foreign minister demands accountability for UN worker’s death in Houthi custody

    
    

        
    
                Yemen’s Foreign Minister Afrah al-Zouba has called for the Houthis to be held accountable for the death of UN human rights employee Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami after more than two years in the group’s custody.

In a post on X, Zouba described his death as a “horrific crime for which the militia bears full responsibility” and urged decisive international action against those responsible.

“His tragedy did not begin with his death; it began with his abduction in June 2024, his enforced disappearance, and the deprivation of his family from communicating with him or knowing his fate,” she said.

Zouba urged the United Nations and its Security Council to pressure the Houthis to release all “abductees”.


مقتل محمد إبراهيم الشامي، موظف مفوضية الأمم المتحدة السامية لحقوق الإنسان، في معتقلات مليشيا الحوثي الإرهابية جريمة مروّعة تتحمّل المليشيا مسؤوليتها الكاملة، وتستوجب تحركاً دولياً حازماً لمحاسبة مرتكبيها وإطلاق بقية المختطفين. مأساته لم تبدأ بوفاته؛ بدأت باختطافه في يونيو 2024، وإخفائه قسرياً، وحرمان أسرته من التواصل معه ومعرفة مصيره. خالص التعازي لأسرته وزملائه؛ رحمه الله وألهم ذويه الصبر والسلوان. لم يكن الشامي أول الضحايا؛ سبقته وفاة موظف في برنامج الأغذية العالمي وآخر في منظمة إنقاذ الطفولة أثناء احتجازهما لدى المليشيا، ولن تنتهي المأساة عنده ما دام الإفلات من العقاب مستمراً. إلى متى تتكرر الإدانات دون إجراءات تحمي المختطفين وتردع الجناة؟ التحرك لإطلاق سراح الموظفين اليمنيين واجب لا يقبل الانتقائية أو التأجيل بدعوى مقتضيات العمل الميداني؛ فقيمة الإنسان لا تتفاوت باختلاف جنسيته أو جهة عمله، وبإنفاذ هذا المبدأ تُقاس مصداقية المنظومة الدولية. من حق أسرة الشامي معرفة الحقيقة عبر تحقيق مستقل تُتاح له سجلات احتجازه وملفه الطبي ويحدد المسؤوليات. وحق بقية المختطفين في الحرية لا ينتظر نتائج أي تحقيق. نطالب الأمم المتحدة ومجلس الأمن بإجراءات تُلزم المليشيا بالإفراج الفوري وغير المشروط عن جميع المختطفين، بمن فيهم موظفو الأمم المتحدة والمنظمات الإنسانية والمجتمع المدني والموظفون المحليون في البعثات الدبلوماسية، وضمان علاجهم وتواصلهم مع أسرهم، وكشف مصير المخفيين قسرياً.
